linkedin:
A Nostr profile image had one place to live: the URL inside a kind 0 JSON document. If that host failed, clients had no standard fallback.

NIP-92 changed on 5 October 2026. A kind 0 event may now carry an imeta tag whose URL exactly matches picture or banner. That tag can add fallback locations, dimensions, a MIME type, SHA-256, blurhash and alt text without moving the canonical URL out of the profile.

The exact match is the important constraint. A redirect target or a URL with a different query string is not the same field. Because kind 0 is replaceable, publishing clients should also preserve imeta only when the image URL is unchanged and drop metadata for images no longer referenced.

We track merged NIPs from the diff and separate what the specification requires from what clients may choose to implement. Which profile-media field would improve your client first: fallback, alt text or dimensions?

This is a backward-compatible format, not a storage guarantee. Old clients can ignore it, fallbacks can still fail, and hashes help only when clients verify them.

nostr:
NIP-92 now lets a kind 0 profile attach imeta to picture and banner. The tag can carry fallback URLs, dimensions, MIME type, SHA-256, blurhash and alt text.

The join is exact: the imeta URL must equal the picture or banner value. A redirect target or changed query string does not match. Publishing clients should preserve metadata for an unchanged image and drop it when the profile stops referencing that image.

Old clients still read the original URL, so the change is backward compatible. It is not a storage promise: fallbacks may fail, every field is optional, and integrity hashes matter only if clients verify them.
